subject: Mutual action plan & performance evaluation blueprint for long-context benchmarks

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Mutual action plan kickoff — performance targets & long-context evals

Hi Sara / Alex,

Great to meet yesterday — thanks for the time. As promised, I put together a short mutual action plan focused specifically on the long-context/large-prompt performance checks you asked about. The MAP in the attached spreadsheet is intentionally narrow: we want to validate end-to-end perf (TTFT, p95 token-latency, steady-state throughput) across the two largest conversation patterns you mentioned: long-history clinical notes (~40k tokens) and episodic prompts (~8–12k tokens).

High-level targets (proposed):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): <= 350 ms for small bursts (<8k prompt), <= 1.2 s for long-history requests (40k) on Dedicated tier.
- Steady-state throughput: 1200 tokens/sec (per GPU) for 8–12k prompt mixes at 4 concurrent sessions.
- Concurrency validation: stable p95 latency at up to 24 concurrent sessions across autoscaled dedicated pools.

Two asks from your side to keep momentum:
1) Confirm the representative prompt sets (I included a sample distribution in the spreadsheet).
2) Grant us a short window to run an initial profiler against a sanitized subset of your data (we only need ~50 sequences from each pattern).

Next steps: If you approve, we’ll run an initial smoke run by Friday, circulate raw CSV results and a short analysis, then iterate on configuration (KV cache settings, batching policies, quantization profile). I’ve looped in Karthik to own the test harness and Marissa to coordinate delivery and procurement items.

Best,
Chloe
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Folks — forwarding Beacon’s OK to proceed. They’ll drop sanitized sequences Monday. Quick summary of the test we should run for the smoke pass (priority):

- Test harness: run benchmark_script.sh (attached) with the following modes:
  * mode A (representative small): 10–12k prompt, batch size 8, 4 concurrent workers, 60s warmup, 5 min measurement.
  * mode B (long-history): 30–40k prompt, continuous KV cache enabled, batch size 1, token-limit set to 2048 output, 3 min measurement.
  * mode C (burst concurrency): mixture of both patterns, step concurrency 4->24 (in 4 increments), observe p50/p90/p95 TTFT and token throughput.

- Metrics to capture in CSV: TTFT (ms), first-100-token latency, tokens/sec (aggregate), GPU utilization, memory headroom, and KV cache hit-rate.

- Target config to test: default KV cache, KV prefetch disabled; then repeat with KV prefetch enabled + async flush to measure trade-offs.

I attached the initial MAP and the quick script. Karthik, can you run the smoke on our internal Dedicated staging cluster (g4dn-like) and drop results back here? Marissa, please prepare an internal one-pager we can share with Beacon procurement on estimated GPU-hours for the full validation.

Thanks — Chloe

Running the smoke today. Quick tech notes before I push results:

- We observed deterministic memory pressure when the pipeline uses kv-cache + quantized int8 kernels on 40k sequences at >8 concurrent sessions; adding async KV eviction reduced OOM spikes. I plan two runs: baseline (no prefetch, no async eviction) and optimized (prefetch + async eviction).
- For the long-history run, we’ll split the 40k token context into rolling chunks that reuse KV state to mimic real-world interactive timelines; TTFT measured at request start (post-auth). We’ll capture both cold-start TTFT and warmed KV TTFT.
- I’ll tag each CSV row with run_id and config labels so Marissa can map to GPU-hour estimates.

Expect CSV and short analysis by EOD Monday. If we see TTFT >1.2s for warmed long-history on baseline, we’ll recommend an early fallback policy (shorter context window + summarization) for production while we tune KV cache parameters.

—Karthik
Senior Systems Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Smoke run results (summary) + revised MAP timeline

Hi all — attaching the raw CSV and a short summary (see below). High level: the optimized KV config (prefetch + async eviction) materially improved TTFT on long-history runs and reduced p95 tail latency under moderate concurrency. Details attached in perf_results_20280810.csv.

Summary (smoke run 2028-08-12):
- Mode A (8–12k prompts): TTFT p50=210ms, p95=360ms; tokens/sec ~1250.
- Mode B (30–40k prompts): cold TTFT p95=1.45s; warmed (KV reused) TTFT p95=980ms with optimized KV config.
- Mode C (burst concurrency 4->24): p95 latency remained under 1.6s up to 16 sessions; at 20–24 sessions we saw p95 jumps to 2.8–3.4s on baseline. Optimized config reduced p95 at 20–24 sessions to ~1.7–2.1s.
- KV cache hit-rate improved from ~65% baseline to ~88% with prefetch tuning; memory overhead increased ~5% but no OOM on staging after eviction tuning.

Recommendation / revised MAP timeline:
- Proceed to a 3-day in-scope validation on your Dedicated region (us-central) starting 2028-09-05.
- Deliverables: full CSV export, runbook for local replay (SRE playbook), and a proposed fallback strategy (context summarization thresholds).
- Procurement asks: estimate ~180 GPU-hours on our Dedicated pool for the full validation; Marissa will provide formal quote.

Sara — would you like us to accelerate the validation earlier? We can carve out 48 GPU-hours sooner if procurement signs the minimal scoped agreement.

Best,
Chloe
